cards.explanation: The answer is to go fight for it with him. Ahab, king of Israel, asks Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, “Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth-gilead?” (1 Kings 22:4). He had just told his servants the city was theirs, and now he turns to his guest with a job. Most hosts show you the guest room, friends. Ahab shows you the battlefield.

The answer is False. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, answers Ahab, “I am as you are, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.” (1 Kings 22:4). He doesn't turn Ahab down. He puts his people and his horses in. Even the horses got signed up without a vote.

The answer is that they say go up, and the Lord will give him the city. About four hundred prophets tell Ahab, “Go up,” and add, “and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king.” (1 Kings 22:6). Four hundred men, and not one of them says stay home. That's a whole room singing the same note.

The answer is True. Jehoshaphat asks, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?” (1 Kings 22:7). Four hundred prophets just said go, and he still wants to ask one more. I think four hundred yeses didn't settle it for him.

The answer is good. Ahab says Micaiah “…never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad.” (1 Kings 22:8). The reason he gives is the kind of news Micaiah brings. That's like being mad at the oven timer for going off.

The answer is True. After Jehoshaphat says, “The king should not say that!” Ahab calls one of his officials and says, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.” (1 Kings 22:9). He says at once, friends. Ahab hates the man and still sends for him fast.

The answer is Arameans. Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, says the LORD declares, “With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.” (1 Kings 22:11). The king of Aram is the one Ahab says he hasn't taken Ramoth-gilead from. Zedekiah brings a prop for the point he's making.

The answer is to speak favorably like the other prophets. The messenger tells Micaiah, “Behold now, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.” (1 Kings 22:13). He's asking Micaiah to match the other prophets. That's a lot of pressure to put on one man.

The answer is True. Micaiah answers, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.” (1 Kings 22:14). That's his answer to a messenger who just asked him to match four hundred prophets. He doesn't promise to match the room. He promises to speak what the LORD tells him.

The answer is go up and triumph, and it surprises you, doesn't it? Micaiah says, “Go up and triumph…” and adds, “…for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.” (1 Kings 22:15). That sounds just like the other prophets. I think Ahab's very next words show he wasn't buying it.

The answer is False. Ahab hears Micaiah say go up and triumph, and he answers, “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?” (1 Kings 22:16). He doesn't take it at Micaiah's word. He pushes for something more.

The answer is a master. The LORD says, “These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.” (1 Kings 22:17). Sheep without a shepherd, people without a master. Both pictures show someone missing at the top.

The answer is True. Ahab says to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?” (1 Kings 22:18). I think he's counting it as proof. He turns to Jehoshaphat like the case is closed.

The answer is who will entice Ahab to fall at Ramoth-gilead. Micaiah says he saw the LORD ask, “Who will entice Ahab to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?” (1 Kings 22:20). It's a heavy scene, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven. Notice that the question is about Ahab and Ramoth-gilead, the very city he wants.

The two words are lying and prophets. The spirit says, “I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.” (1 Kings 22:22). That's why Micaiah is telling Ahab something different from the four hundred. These are the same prophets who all said go up. Micaiah is pulling back the curtain on the whole room.

The answer is True. The LORD says to the spirit, “You will surely entice him and prevail... Go and do it.” (1 Kings 22:22). It's a heavy moment in the vision, so I'll just let the words stand. Micaiah tells Ahab this in the open, in front of both kings.

The answer is that Zedekiah will see on the day he hides in an inner room. Micaiah answers Zedekiah, “You will soon see, on that day when you go and hide in an inner room.” (1 Kings 22:25). Zedekiah had just struck him in the face, and this is his answer. He doesn't say what that day will look like, and I won't guess.

The answer is to put him in prison until Ahab returns. Ahab says, “Put this man in prison and feed him only bread and water until I return safely.” (1 Kings 22:27). Ahab's order has an end date in it, and it's his own safe return. The order also says to feed Micaiah only bread and water.

The answer is True. Micaiah says, “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.” (1 Kings 22:28). He says it right after the king orders him to prison. He puts the whole test on one thing: whether Ahab returns safely.
